scenes.heading: CAN AI CLICK YOUR APPS?
scenes.say: Want your AI agent to click through your desktop apps?

scenes.heading: ONE LINE TO INSTALL
scenes.say: Agent-desktop gives your agent a way in. With Node.js and npm installed, run npm install -g agent-desktop.

scenes.heading: SNAPSHOT THE ACCESSIBLE APP
scenes.say: Take a snapshot of an app. It returns accessible elements and a ref for each one the agent can use.

scenes.heading: CLICK A REF, NOT A PIXEL
scenes.say: Pass that ref to the click command, then take another snapshot to check what changed.

scenes.heading: STALE REFS RETRY
scenes.say: If a ref goes stale after the UI changes, take a fresh snapshot and use its new refs.

scenes.heading: THREE DESKTOP PLATFORMS
scenes.say: It works on macOS, Windows, and Linux; your agent still has to run the loop.
Which desktop task would you automate first? Comment DESKTOP and I'll pin the link.

idea: agent-desktop lets an agent read and act on desktop apps through the OS accessibility tree.

claims.text: Install it with one npm command.
A snapshot returns accessible elements with refs for elements the agent can act on.
An agent can click a ref and take another snapshot to verify.
A stale or ambiguous ref needs a fresh snapshot and new refs.
